_about: Historical eras and archaeological finds that help set Scripture in context. Written for this app as a study aid with cautious language; dates are conventional estimates and several are debated. Verify details with a reputable archaeological reference before quoting.

eras.title: The patriarchs
eras.summary: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph move between Mesopotamia, Canaan and Egypt.
eras.context: Dating the patriarchs is uncertain and debated; Genesis gives no absolute dates.

eras.title: Exodus and wilderness
eras.dates: c. 13th century BC (a common but debated dating)
eras.summary: Israel leaves Egypt, receives the law at Sinai and wanders forty years.
eras.context: The date of the Exodus is much debated (15th vs 13th century BC are the leading proposals).

eras.title: Settlement and judges
eras.summary: Israel enters Canaan, and judges such as Deborah, Gideon and Samson arise.
eras.context: The Merneptah Stele (c. 1208 BC), an Egyptian victory inscription, is the earliest known mention of “Israel” outside the Bible.

eras.title: United monarchy
eras.summary: Saul, David and Solomon; Jerusalem becomes the capital and the Temple is built.
eras.context: The Tel Dan inscription (9th century BC) mentions a “house of David.”

eras.title: Divided kingdom
eras.summary: Israel in the north and Judah in the south; prophets Elijah, Elisha, Amos, Hosea, Isaiah.
eras.context: Assyrian records describe Israel’s defeat and the fall of Samaria in 722 BC.

eras.title: Judah, exile and return
eras.summary: Assyria threatens Jerusalem; Babylon destroys the Temple in 586 BC; the exiles return under Persian rule.
eras.context: Sennacherib’s Prism records the 701 BC siege of Jerusalem; the Cyrus Cylinder reflects Persian policy toward exiled peoples.

eras.title: The Second Temple period
eras.summary: Persian, Greek and Roman rule; the Maccabean revolt; Herod rebuilds the Temple.
eras.context: Writings from Qumran (the Dead Sea Scrolls) and Josephus describe Jewish life in this age.

eras.title: The time of Jesus
eras.summary: Jesus is born under Roman rule, ministers in Galilee and Judea, and is crucified under Pontius Pilate.
eras.context: A stone inscription found at Caesarea names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea.

eras.title: The early Church
eras.summary: The gospel spreads from Jerusalem through the Roman empire.
eras.context: An inscription at Delphi dating the proconsulship of Gallio helps fix the date of Paul’s stay in Corinth (Acts 18:12).

finds.name: Merneptah Stele
finds.note: The earliest known mention of “Israel” outside the Bible, in a victory hymn of Pharaoh Merneptah.

finds.name: Tel Dan Inscription
finds.note: An Aramaic inscription that most scholars read as mentioning the “house of David.”

finds.name: Siloam Tunnel and Inscription
finds.note: A water tunnel cut through rock, with a Hebrew inscription describing its completion, widely linked to Hezekiah’s work.

finds.name: Sennacherib’s Prism
finds.where: Nineveh (now in the British Museum and elsewhere)
finds.note: The Assyrian king’s account of his campaign and his siege of Jerusalem.

finds.name: Cyrus Cylinder
finds.note: A Persian royal text describing Cyrus’ policy of returning peoples to their homelands and restoring their temples; it does not mention Jerusalem, but it fits the policy behind Ezra 1.

finds.name: Dead Sea Scrolls
finds.note: The oldest surviving copies of most books of the Hebrew Bible, including a nearly complete Isaiah scroll, and writings of a Jewish community.

finds.name: Pilate Stone
finds.note: A Latin dedication inscription naming Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea.

finds.name: Gallio Inscription
finds.note: An inscription from the emperor Claudius that helps date Gallio’s time as proconsul of Achaia, and so Paul’s time in Corinth.

finds.name: Erastus Inscription
finds.note: A paved-area inscription naming an Erastus as aedile; some scholars link him with the Erastus of Romans 16:23.

finds.name: Pool of Siloam
finds.note: Excavations have uncovered a large stepped pool identified with the Pool of Siloam.

finds.name: Capernaum synagogue and houses
finds.note: Remains of a synagogue and of village houses; beneath a later church is a house venerated since early Christian times as Peter’s.

finds.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
finds.note: The church built over the traditional site of Jesus’ crucifixion and burial; excavation shows the area was a quarry used for tombs in the first century.
